text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Parties in ruling coalition try to contain their row over tax policy and the budget.
- Six leading economic institutes predict 2.5 percent GDP growth for Germany in 1997.
- German delegation in Indonesia signs contracts for 25 projects.
- Employers and trade unions agree regional wage deal for 1997 in southwest Germany will be transferred to the rest of the country.
- German trade with eastern Europe on the increase, economics ministry says.
HANDELSBLATT
- Six institutes say Germany will miss budget deficit target laid down in Maastricht treaty for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
- State of Bavaria says it ready to abandon wage agreements with public sector workers.
- East German economy consolidating its recovery, Handelsblatt indicator shows.
- Banks believe Deutsche Telekom share offer will be oversubscribed.
- HBV, DPG and IG Medien trade unions form alliance to work more closely together.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Coalition parties try to defuse tension over budget row.
- OeTV white collar union warns against abandoning current public sector wage agreements.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem protests against Health Minister Horst Seehofer's plans to cut back on treatment paid for by public health insurance funds.
DIE WELT
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) call emergency parliamentary debate for Wednesday on government financial policy.
- Statistics show strong imbalance remains in trade between western and eastern Germany. East German industry announces "export offensive" to try to narrow the gap.
- Opposition Greens agrue about whether German troops should take part in new peace mission to Bosnia.
